title: Shortest Subarray With Large Enough Sum

concept.title: A window that grows and shrinks
body: When all numbers are **positive**, adding an element to a window can only increase its sum and removing one can only decrease it. So you can grow the window on the right until the sum is big enough, then shrink it from the left as far as the sum stays big enough, recording the length every time.

body.code:
l = total = 0
for r in range(n):
    total += a[r]
    while total >= s:
        best = min(best, r - l + 1)
        total -= a[l]
        l += 1

body: Both pointers only move forward, so each element enters and leaves the window once: O(n). With negative numbers this idea breaks, because shrinking could increase the sum.

statement: Given `n` positive integers and a number `s`, find the length of the shortest block of consecutive elements whose sum is at least `s`. If no block has such a sum, print 0.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` positive integers.

examples.note: The block 4 3 has sum 7 and length 2.

hints: All numbers are positive, so a longer window never has a smaller sum.
Grow the window to the right; while its sum is at least `s`, record its length and shrink it from the left.

explanation: The right pointer adds elements; whenever the sum reaches `s` the left pointer removes elements as long as possible. The smallest recorded length is the answer.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, s = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

best = 0
l = 0
total = 0
for rr in range(n):
    total += a[rr]
    while total >= s:
        length = rr - l + 1
        if best == 0 or length < best:
            best = length
        total -= a[l]
        l += 1
print(best)
